Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 93, verse 1–11 (part 1 of 2):

Tafsir of Surat al-Duha (The Morning Brightness)
It is a Meccan surah.

We have related through the chain of Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Bazzah al-Muqri', who said: I recited to Ikrimah ibn Sulayman, and he informed me that he had recited to Isma'il ibn Qustantin and Shibl ibn Abbad. When I reached "Wa'l-Duha," they said to me: "Pronounce the takbir until you finish with the ending of every surah, for we recited to Ibn Kathir and he commanded us to do so. He informed us that he had recited to Mujahid, who commanded him to do so. Mujahid informed him that he had recited to Ibn Abbas, who commanded him to do so. Ibn Abbas informed him that he had recited to Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who commanded him to do so. Ubayy informed him that he had recited to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who commanded him to do so" [[Also related by al-Hafiz al-Dhahabi in Mizan al-I'tidal (1/145), then he said: "This is a strange hadith, and it is among what was disapproved of from al-Bazzi. Abu Hatim said: This is munkar."]].

This is a sunnah transmitted uniquely by Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Bazzi, a descendant of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, who was an imam in the readings (qira'at). As for hadith, Abu Hatim al-Razi weakened him and said: "I do not narrate from him." Likewise Abu Ja'far al-Uqayli said: "He is munkar al-hadith." However, Shaykh Shihab al-Din Abu Shamah, in his commentary on al-Shatibiyyah, reported from al-Shafi'i that he heard a man pronounce this takbir in prayer, and said to him: "You have done well and you have followed the sunnah." This implies the soundness of this hadith.

Then the reciters differed regarding the place of this takbir and its manner. Some said: one pronounces it from the end of "Wa'l-layli idha yaghsha," and others said: from the end of "Wa'l-Duha." Regarding the manner of the takbir, according to some, one says "Allahu akbar" and stops; and among them are those who say "Allahu akbar, la ilaha illa Allah, wa-Allahu akbar."

Al-Farra' mentioned, regarding the occasion of the takbir at the beginning of Surat al-Duha, that when revelation was delayed from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and paused for that period, [then] [[addition from M.]] the angel came to him and revealed to him "Wa'l-Duha, wa'l-layli idha saja," the surah in its entirety, and he pronounced takbir out of joy and gladness. This has not been related with a chain by which it may be judged sound or weak, and Allah knows best [[The correct view is that nothing authentic has been established on this from the Prophet (ﷺ) or his Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, and what has been narrated concerning it is not a sound proof. Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah spoke strongly about this takbir in al-Fatawa (13/417-419). See also al-Adab al-Shar'iyyah by Ibn Muflih (2/310) and Marwiyyat du'a khatm al-Qur'an by Bakr Abu Zayd (p. 6), from whose book I benefited, may Allah reward him well.]].

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful

* *

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Nu'aym related to us, Sufyan related to us, from al-Aswad ibn Qays, who said: I heard Jundub say: The Prophet (ﷺ) became ill and did not rise [for prayer] for a night or two nights. A woman came and said: "O Muhammad, I do not see your devil except that he has forsaken you." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it is still, your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you﴾ [[al-Musnad (4/312).]].

It was related by al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir, through several routes, from al-Aswad ibn Qays, from Jundub, he being Ibn Abdullah al-Bajali thumma al-Alaqi [[In A: "al-Alqami."]], with this wording [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (1124, 1125, 4983, 4950, 4951); Sahih Muslim, no. (1797); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3345); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11681); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (3250).]]. In the narration of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah from al-Aswad ibn Qays: he heard Jundub say: "Jibril was late in coming to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so the polytheists said: 'Muhammad has been forsaken.' So Allah revealed: ﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it is still, your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you﴾" [[This narration is in Muslim and al-Tirmidhi.]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj and Amr ibn Abdullah [[In A: "Amr ibn Abdullah ibn Abdullah al-Awdi."]] al-Awdi related to us, both saying: Abu Usamah related to us, Sufyan related to me, al-Aswad ibn Qays related to me, that he heard Jundub say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was struck by a stone on his finger, and he said:

"Are you but a finger that bled,
and in the way of Allah what you have suffered?"

He said: So he remained a night or two or three without rising, and a woman said to him: "I do not see your devil except that he has forsaken you [[In M: "has forsaken you."]]." Then there was revealed: ﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it is still, your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you﴾. The wording is that of Abu Sa'id.

It has been said: this woman was Umm Jamil, the wife of Abu Lahab. It is also mentioned that his finger, upon him be peace, bled. As for his statement, this verse which happened to be metrical, it is established in the two Sahihs [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (2802); Sahih Muslim, no. (1796).]]. But what is strange here is making it the cause of his ceasing to pray at night and the descent of this surah. As for what Ibn Jarir related:

Ibn Abi al-Shawarib related to us, Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad related to us, Sulayman al-Shaybani related to us, from Abd Allah ibn Shaddad: that Khadijah said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "I do not see your Lord except that He has become averse to you." So Allah revealed: ﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it is still, your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you﴾.

He also said: Abu Kurayb related to us, Waki' related to us, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, who said: Jibril was late with the Prophet (ﷺ), so he grieved greatly, and Khadijah said: "I see that your Lord has become averse to you, given what we see of your grief." He said: So there was revealed ﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it is still, your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you﴾ to its end [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/148).]].

This is a mursal hadith through these two routes, and perhaps the mention of Khadijah is not preserved, or she said it in a manner of regret and sorrow, and Allah knows best.

Some of the predecessors, among them Ibn Ishaq, mentioned that this surah is what Jibril revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he appeared to him in his true form, which Allah created him upon, drew near to him and descended, hovering over him while he was at al-Abtah, ﴿So He revealed to His servant what He revealed﴾ [al-Najm: 10]. He said: He said to him this surah: ﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it is still﴾.

Al-Awfi related from Ibn Abbas: When the Qur'an was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Jibril was late for days, so he was distressed by this, and the polytheists said: "His Lord has forsaken him and detested him." So Allah revealed: ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you﴾.

This is an oath by Him, exalted is He, by the morning brightness and what He placed in it of light, ﴿and by the night when it is still﴾, i.e., when it becomes calm and dark and black. This was said by Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, Ibn Zayd and others. This is clear evidence of the power of the Creator of this and that, as He said: ﴿By the night when it covers, and by the day when it appears in brightness﴾ [al-Layl: 1, 2], and He said: ﴿He is the Splitter of the dawn, and has made the night for rest, and the sun and the moon for reckoning. That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾ [al-An'am: 96].

* *

His statement: ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you﴾, i.e., He has not left you; ﴿nor has He detested you﴾, i.e., He has not hated you; ﴿And the Hereafter is better for you than the first﴾, i.e., the Abode of the Hereafter is better for you than this abode. For this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was the most ascetic of people regarding this world, and the greatest in casting it aside, as is well known [necessarily] [[addition from M.]] from his biography. When, upon him be peace, was given the choice at the end of his life between remaining in this world until its end and then Paradise, or proceeding to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, he chose what is with Allah over this lowly world.

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid related to us, al-Mas'udi related to us, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, from Alqamah, from Abd Allah, that is Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) lay down on a mat, and it left its mark on his side. When he awoke, I began to wipe his side and said: "O Messenger of Allah, would you not let us know so that we could spread something for you over the mat?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "What have I to do with this world? My likeness and the likeness of this world is that of a rider who rests in the shade of a tree, then goes on and leaves it."

It was related by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, from the hadith of al-Mas'udi with it [[al-Musnad (1/391); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (2377); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (4109).]]. Al-Tirmidhi said: hasan sahih.

* *

His statement: ﴿And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be content﴾, i.e., in the Hereafter He will give him until he is pleased regarding his community, and in what He has prepared for him of honour, and of its totality is the river of Kawthar, whose banks are domes of hollow pearls, and whose clay is [of] [[addition from A.]] pungent musk, as will come.

Imam Abu Umar al-Awza'i said, from Isma'il ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Abi al-Muhajir al-Makhzumi, from Ali ibn Abd Allah ibn Abbas, from his father, who said: What would be opened for his community after him was displayed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), treasure after treasure, and he was pleased by this, so Allah revealed: ﴿And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be content﴾, and He gave him in Paradise a thousand thousand palaces, in each palace what befits him of spouses and servants. Ibn Jarir related it through this route, and this is a sound chain to Ibn Abbas, and such a statement is only made on the basis of revelation.

Al-Suddi said, from Ibn Abbas: Among the contentment of Muhammad (ﷺ) is that none of the people of his household enter the Fire. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related it.

Al-Hasan said: By that is meant intercession. Likewise said Abu Ja'far al-Baqir.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah said: Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham related to us, from Ali ibn Salih, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, from Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "We are a household whom Allah has chosen the Hereafter for over this world. ﴿And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be content﴾" [[al-Baghawi related it in Sharh al-Sunnah (14/248) through the route of Ibn Abi Shaybah, without the verse; Ibn Abi Shaybah related it in al-Musannaf (15/236) by this route without mentioning the verse, and perhaps its mention occurred in the book of tafsir; Ibn Majah related it in al-Sunan, no. (4082), from Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah, from Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham with it, and al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/262): "This chain contains Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad al-Kufi, about whom there is disagreement."]].

Then He, exalted, said, enumerating His blessings upon His servant and Messenger Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him: ﴿Did He not find you an orphan and give you shelter?﴾ This is because his father died while he was in his mother's womb; and it has been said: after he was born, upon him be peace. Then his mother Aminah bint Wahb died when he was six years old. Then he was under the care of his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib until he died when he was eight years old, and then his uncle Abu Talib took charge of him. He continued to protect him, support him, raise his status, honour him, and restrain from him the harm of his people after Allah sent him as a messenger at the age of forty, although Abu Talib was upon the religion of his people of idol worship. All of this was by the decree of Allah and His excellent management, until Abu Talib died shortly before the Hijrah, and the foolish and ignorant among the Quraysh then pressed upon him. So Allah chose for him the Hijrah from among them to the land of the Ansar, of the Aws and the Khazraj, as Allah carried out His sunnah in the most complete and perfect manner. When he reached them, they sheltered him, supported him, protected him, and fought before him, may Allah be pleased with them all. All of this was from Allah's preservation of him, His guardianship, and His care for him.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And He found you lost and guided you﴾, like His saying: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command. You did not know what the Book was, nor what faith was, but We made it a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants. And indeed you guide to a straight path﴾ [Ash-Shura: 52]. Among them are those who said: "[That] [[Addition from M.]] what is meant by this is that he, peace be upon him, got lost in the mountain paths of Makkah when he was a child, and then returned." It was also said: he got lost while he was with his uncle on the road to Syria, riding a she-camel at night, and Iblis came to turn her away from the road. Then Jibril came, and blew into Iblis a blast by which he was sent off to Abyssinia, and then he turned the mount back onto the road. Al-Baghawi related both accounts.

*  *

And His saying: ﴿And He found you in need and enriched you﴾, meaning: you were poor and had dependants, and Allah made you independent of anyone other than Him. Thus He combined for him the two stations: the patient poor and the thankful rich, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him.

Qatadah said concerning His saying: ﴿Did He not find you an orphan and give you refuge, and find you lost and guide you, and find you in need and enrich you?﴾ He said: These were the stations of the Messenger ﷺ before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent him as a prophet. Related by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim.

In the two Sahihs [through the chain of Abd al-Razzaq], from Ma'mar, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: "This is what Abu Hurairah related to us, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Wealth is not having abundant goods, but true wealth is the wealth of the soul.'" [[I have not located it in the two Sahihs through this chain; it has come in them through other routes from Abu Hurairah. See Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6446) and Sahih Muslim no. (1051).]]

In Sahih Muslim, from Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "He has succeeded who embraces Islam, is provided with sufficiency, and Allah makes him content with what He has given him." [Sahih Muslim no. (1054).]

Then He said: ﴿So as for the orphan, do not oppress him﴾, meaning: just as you were an orphan and Allah gave you refuge, do not oppress the orphan, that is, do not humiliate him, rebuke him or disgrace him, but rather be kind to him and treat him gently.

Qatadah said: Be to the orphan like a compassionate father.

﴿And as for the one who asks, do not repel him﴾, meaning: and just as you were lost and Allah guided you, do not rebuke the one who asks you about knowledge and seeks guidance.

Ibn Ishaq said: ﴿And as for the one who asks, do not repel him﴾, meaning: do not be tyrannical, nor arrogant, nor foul-mouthed, nor harsh toward the weak among the servants of Allah.

Qatadah said: It means to turn away the poor man with mercy and gentleness.

﴿And as for the blessing of your Lord, proclaim it﴾, meaning: and just as you were poor and in need and Allah enriched you, so proclaim the blessing of Allah upon you, as is found in the prophetic supplication transmitted: "And make us thankful for Your blessings, praising them, accepting them, and completing them upon us."

Ibn Jarir said: Yaqub related to me, Ibn Ulayyah related to us, Sa'id ibn Iyas al-Juraири related to us, from Abu Nadrah, who said: The Muslims used to hold that among the thanks due for blessings is to speak of them.

Abdullah ibn al-Imam Ahmad said: Mansur ibn Abi Muzahim related to us, al-Jarrah ibn Malih related to us, from Abu Abd al-Rahman, from al-Sha'bi, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said from the pulpit: "Whoever does not thank for little does not thank for much, and whoever does not thank people does not thank Allah. Speaking of the blessing of Allah is thanks, and leaving it is disbelief. Community is mercy, and division is punishment." [Zawa'id al-Musnad (4/278).] Its chain is weak.

In the two Sahihs, from Anas, that the Muhajirun said: "O Messenger of Allah, the Ansar have taken all the reward." He said: "No, as long as you pray for them and praise them." [[I have not located it in the two Sahihs; Imam Ahmad related it in al-Musnad (3/200).]]

Abu Dawud said: Muslim ibn Ibrahim related to us, al-Rabi' ibn Muslim related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: "He who does not thank people does not thank Allah."

al-Tirmidhi also related it from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn al-Mubarak, from al-Rabi' ibn Muslim [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4811) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1954).]], and said: Sahih.

Abu Dawud said: Abdullah ibn al-Jarrah related to us, Jarir related to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: "Whoever is tested with a trial and mentions it has thanked for it, and whoever conceals it has disbelieved in it." Abu Dawud alone related it. [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4814).]]

Abu Dawud said: Musaddad related to us, Bishr [[In A: "Bashir".]] related to us, Umarah ibn Ghaziyyah related to us, a man of my people related to me, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever is given a gift and finds [the means], let him repay it; if he does not find [the means], let him praise it. Whoever praises it has thanked it, and whoever conceals it has disbelieved in it." Abu Dawud said: Yahya ibn Ayyub related it from Umarah ibn Ghaziyyah, from Shurahbil, from Jabir, [but] they disliked it and did not name him. Abu Dawud alone related it. [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4813).]]

Mujahid said: It means the prophethood which your Lord has given you. In another report from him: the Qur'an.

Layth said, from a man, from al-Hasan ibn Ali: ﴿And as for the blessing of your Lord, proclaim it﴾, he said: Whatever good you do, tell your brothers about it.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Whatever blessing and honour from Allah has come to you in the form of prophethood, proclaim it, mention it, and call to it. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ began to mention the blessing Allah had bestowed upon him of prophethood, secretly, to those among his family in whom he was at ease, and prayer was made obligatory upon him, so he prayed.

End of the tafsir of Surah "al-Duha" [and to Allah belongs all praise]. [[Addition from A.]]

Tafsir of Surat al-Duha (The Morning Brightness)
It is a Meccan surah.

We have related through the chain of Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Bazzah al-Muqri', who said: I recited to Ikrimah ibn Sulayman, and he informed me that he had recited to Isma'il ibn Qustantin and Shibl ibn Abbad. When I reached "Wa'l-Duha," they said to me: "Pronounce the takbir until you finish with the ending of every surah, for we recited to Ibn Kathir and he commanded us to do so. He informed us that he had recited to Mujahid, who commanded him to do so. Mujahid informed him that he had recited to Ibn Abbas, who commanded him to do so. Ibn Abbas informed him that he had recited to Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who commanded him to do so. Ubayy informed him that he had recited to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who commanded him to do so" [[Also related by al-Hafiz al-Dhahabi in Mizan al-I'tidal (1/145), then he said: "This is a strange hadith, and it is among what was disapproved of from al-Bazzi. Abu Hatim said: This is munkar."]].

This is a sunnah transmitted uniquely by Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Bazzi, a descendant of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, who was an imam in the readings (qira'at). As for hadith, Abu Hatim al-Razi weakened him and said: "I do not narrate from him." Likewise Abu Ja'far al-Uqayli said: "He is munkar al-hadith." However, Shaykh Shihab al-Din Abu Shamah, in his commentary on al-Shatibiyyah, reported from al-Shafi'i that he heard a man pronounce this takbir in prayer, and said to him: "You have done well and you have followed the sunnah." This implies the soundness of this hadith.

Then the reciters differed regarding the place of this takbir and its manner. Some said: one pronounces it from the end of "Wa'l-layli idha yaghsha," and others said: from the end of "Wa'l-Duha." Regarding the manner of the takbir, according to some, one says "Allahu akbar" and stops; and among them are those who say "Allahu akbar, la ilaha illa Allah, wa-Allahu akbar."

Al-Farra' mentioned, regarding the occasion of the takbir at the beginning of Surat al-Duha, that when revelation was delayed from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and paused for that period, [then] [[addition from M.]] the angel came to him and revealed to him "Wa'l-Duha, wa'l-layli idha saja," the surah in its entirety, and he pronounced takbir out of joy and gladness. Tafsir of Surat al-Duha (The Morning Brightness)
It is a Meccan surah.

We have related through the chain of Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Bazzah al-Muqri', who said: I recited to Ikrimah ibn Sulayman, and he informed me that he had recited to Isma'il ibn Qustantin and Shibl ibn Abbad. When I reached "Wa'l-Duha," they said to me: "Pronounce the takbir until you finish with the ending of every surah, for we recited to Ibn Kathir and he commanded us to do so. He informed us that he had recited to Mujahid, who commanded him to do so. Mujahid informed him that he had recited to Ibn Abbas, who commanded him to do so. Ibn Abbas informed him that he had recited to Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who commanded him to do so. Ubayy informed him that he had recited to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who commanded him to do so" [[Also related by al-Hafiz al-Dhahabi in Mizan al-I'tidal (1/145), then he said: "This is a strange hadith, and it is among what was disapproved of from al-Bazzi. Abu Hatim said: This is munkar."]].

This is a sunnah transmitted uniquely by Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Bazzi, a descendant of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, who was an imam in the readings (qira'at). As for hadith, Abu Hatim al-Razi weakened him and said: "I do not narrate from him." Likewise Abu Ja'far al-Uqayli said: "He is munkar al-hadith." However, Shaykh Shihab al-Din Abu Shamah, in his commentary on al-Shatibiyyah, reported from al-Shafi'i that he heard a man pronounce this takbir in prayer, and said to him: "You have done well and you have followed the sunnah." This implies the soundness of this hadith.

Then the reciters differed regarding the place of this takbir and its manner. Some said: one pronounces it from the end of "Wa'l-layli idha yaghsha," and others said: from the end of "Wa'l-Duha." Regarding the manner of the takbir, according to some, one says "Allahu akbar" and stops; and among them are those who say "Allahu akbar, la ilaha illa Allah, wa-Allahu akbar."

Al-Farra' mentioned, regarding the occasion of the takbir at the beginning of Surat al-Duha, that when revelation was delayed from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and paused for that period, [then] [[addition from M.]] the angel came to him and revealed to him "Wa'l-Duha, wa'l-layli idha saja," the surah in its entirety, and he pronounced takbir out of joy and gladness. This has not been related with a chain by which it may be judged sound or weak, and Allah knows best [[The correct view is that nothing authentic has been established on this from the Prophet (ﷺ) or his Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, and what has been narrated concerning it is not a sound proof. Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah spoke strongly about this takbir in al-Fatawa (13/417-419). In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful

* *

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Nu'aym related to us, Sufyan related to us, from al-Aswad ibn Qays, who said: I heard Jundub say: The Prophet (ﷺ) became ill and did not rise [for prayer] for a night or two nights. A woman came and said: "O Muhammad, I do not see your devil except that he has forsaken you." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it is still, your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you﴾ [[al-Musnad (4/312).]].

It was related by al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir, through several routes, from al-Aswad ibn Qays, from Jundub, he being Ibn Abdullah al-Bajali thumma al-Alaqi [[In A: "al-Alqami."]], with this wording [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. "Are you but a finger that bled,
and in the way of Allah what you have suffered?"

That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾ [al-An'am: 96].

* *

For this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was the most ascetic of people regarding this world, and the greatest in casting it aside, as is well known [necessarily] [[addition from M.]] from his biography. When, upon him be peace, was given the choice at the end of his life between remaining in this world until its end and then Paradise, or proceeding to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, he chose what is with Allah over this lowly world.

When he awoke, I began to wipe his side and said: "O Messenger of Allah, would you not let us know so that we could spread something for you over the mat?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "What have I to do with this world? My likeness and the likeness of this world is that of a rider who rests in the shade of a tree, then goes on and leaves it."

It was related by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, from the hadith of al-Mas'udi with it [[al-Musnad (1/391); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (2377); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (4109).]]. Al-Tirmidhi said: hasan sahih.

* *

Al-Suddi said, from Ibn Abbas: Among the contentment of Muhammad (ﷺ) is that none of the people of his household enter the Fire. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related it.

Al-Hasan said: By that is meant intercession. Likewise said Abu Ja'far al-Baqir.

*  *

Qatadah said concerning His saying: ﴿Did He not find you an orphan and give you refuge, and find you lost and guide you, and find you in need and enrich you?﴾ He said: These were the stations of the Messenger ﷺ before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent him as a prophet. In Sahih Muslim, from Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "He has succeeded who embraces Islam, is provided with sufficiency, and Allah makes him content with what He has given him." [Sahih Muslim no. (1054).]

Qatadah said: Be to the orphan like a compassionate father.

﴿And as for the one who asks, do not repel him﴾, meaning: and just as you were lost and Allah guided you, do not rebuke the one who asks you about knowledge and seeks guidance.

Ibn Ishaq said: ﴿And as for the one who asks, do not repel him﴾, meaning: do not be tyrannical, nor arrogant, nor foul-mouthed, nor harsh toward the weak among the servants of Allah.

Qatadah said: It means to turn away the poor man with mercy and gentleness.

﴿And as for the blessing of your Lord, proclaim it﴾, meaning: and just as you were poor and in need and Allah enriched you, so proclaim the blessing of Allah upon you, as is found in the prophetic supplication transmitted: "And make us thankful for Your blessings, praising them, accepting them, and completing them upon us."

Abdullah ibn al-Imam Ahmad said: Mansur ibn Abi Muzahim related to us, al-Jarrah ibn Malih related to us, from Abu Abd al-Rahman, from al-Sha'bi, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said from the pulpit: "Whoever does not thank for little does not thank for much, and whoever does not thank people does not thank Allah. Speaking of the blessing of Allah is thanks, and leaving it is disbelief. Community is mercy, and division is punishment." [Zawa'id al-Musnad (4/278).] Its chain is weak.

In the two Sahihs, from Anas, that the Muhajirun said: "O Messenger of Allah, the Ansar have taken all the reward." He said: "No, as long as you pray for them and praise them." [[I have not located it in the two Sahihs; Imam Ahmad related it in al-Musnad (3/200).]]

Abu Dawud said: Muslim ibn Ibrahim related to us, al-Rabi' ibn Muslim related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: "He who does not thank people does not thank Allah."

Abu Dawud said: Abdullah ibn al-Jarrah related to us, Jarir related to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: "Whoever is tested with a trial and mentions it has thanked for it, and whoever conceals it has disbelieved in it." Abu Dawud alone related it. [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4814).]]

Abu Dawud said: Musaddad related to us, Bishr [[In A: "Bashir".]] related to us, Umarah ibn Ghaziyyah related to us, a man of my people related to me, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever is given a gift and finds [the means], let him repay it; if he does not find [the means], let him praise it. Whoever praises it has thanked it, and whoever conceals it has disbelieved in it." Abu Dawud said: Yahya ibn Ayyub related it from Umarah ibn Ghaziyyah, from Shurahbil, from Jabir, [but] they disliked it and did not name him. Abu Dawud alone related it. [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4813).]]

Mujahid said: It means the prophethood which your Lord has given you. In another report from him: the Qur'an.

Layth said, from a man, from al-Hasan ibn Ali: ﴿And as for the blessing of your Lord, proclaim it﴾, he said: Whatever good you do, tell your brothers about it.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Whatever blessing and honour from Allah has come to you in the form of prophethood, proclaim it, mention it, and call to it. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ began to mention the blessing Allah had bestowed upon him of prophethood, secretly, to those among his family in whom he was at ease, and prayer was made obligatory upon him, so he prayed.

Tafsir of Surat al-Duha (The Morning Brightness)
It is a Meccan surah.

We have related through the chain of Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Bazzah al-Muqri', who said: I recited to Ikrimah ibn Sulayman, and he informed me that he had recited to Isma'il ibn Qustantin and Shibl ibn Abbad. When I reached "Wa'l-Duha," they said to me: "Pronounce the takbir until you finish with the ending of every surah, for we recited to Ibn Kathir and he commanded us to do so. He informed us that he had recited to Mujahid, who commanded him to do so. Mujahid informed him that he had recited to Ibn Abbas, who commanded him to do so. Ibn Abbas informed him that he had recited to Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who commanded him to do so. Ubayy informed him that he had recited to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who commanded him to do so" [[Also related by al-Hafiz al-Dhahabi in Mizan al-I'tidal (1/145), then he said: "This is a strange hadith, and it is among what was disapproved of from al-Bazzi. Abu Hatim said: This is munkar."]].

This is a sunnah transmitted uniquely by Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Bazzi, a descendant of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, who was an imam in the readings (qira'at). As for hadith, Abu Hatim al-Razi weakened him and said: "I do not narrate from him." Likewise Abu Ja'far al-Uqayli said: "He is munkar al-hadith." However, Shaykh Shihab al-Din Abu Shamah, in his commentary on al-Shatibiyyah, reported from al-Shafi'i that he heard a man pronounce this takbir in prayer, and said to him: "You have done well and you have followed the sunnah." This implies the soundness of this hadith.

Then the reciters differed regarding the place of this takbir and its manner. Some said: one pronounces it from the end of "Wa'l-layli idha yaghsha," and others said: from the end of "Wa'l-Duha." Regarding the manner of the takbir, according to some, one says "Allahu akbar" and stops; and among them are those who say "Allahu akbar, la ilaha illa Allah, wa-Allahu akbar."

Al-Farra' mentioned, regarding the occasion of the takbir at the beginning of Surat al-Duha, that when revelation was delayed from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and paused for that period, [then] [[addition from M.]] the angel came to him and revealed to him "Wa'l-Duha, wa'l-layli idha saja," the surah in its entirety, and he pronounced takbir out of joy and gladness. This has not been related with a chain by which it may be judged sound or weak, and Allah knows best [[The correct view is that nothing authentic has been established on this from the Prophet (ﷺ) or his Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, and what has been narrated concerning it is not a sound proof. Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah spoke strongly about this takbir in al-Fatawa (13/417-419). We have related through the chain of Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Bazzah al-Muqri', who said: I recited to Ikrimah ibn Sulayman, and he informed me that he had recited to Isma'il ibn Qustantin and Shibl ibn Abbad. When I reached "Wa'l-Duha," they said to me: "Pronounce the takbir until you finish with the ending of every surah, for we recited to Ibn Kathir and he commanded us to do so. He informed us that he had recited to Mujahid, who commanded him to do so. Mujahid informed him that he had recited to Ibn Abbas, who commanded him to do so. Ibn Abbas informed him that he had recited to Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who commanded him to do so. Ubayy informed him that he had recited to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who commanded him to do so" [[Also related by al-Hafiz al-Dhahabi in Mizan al-I'tidal (1/145), then he said: "This is a strange hadith, and it is among what was disapproved of from al-Bazzi. Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah spoke strongly about this takbir in al-Fatawa (13/417-419). "Are you but a finger that bled,

As for his statement, this verse which happened to be metrical, it is established in the two Sahihs [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (2802); Sahih Muslim, no. (1796).]]. But what is strange here is making it the cause of his ceasing to pray at night and the descent of this surah. As for what Ibn Jarir related:

Then he was under the care of his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib until he died when he was eight years old, and then his uncle Abu Talib took charge of him. He continued to protect him, support him, raise his status, honour him, and restrain from him the harm of his people after Allah sent him as a messenger at the age of forty, although Abu Talib was upon the religion of his people of idol worship. (1124, 1125, 4983, 4950, 4951); Sahih Muslim, no. (1797); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3345); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11681); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (3250).]]. In the narration of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah from al-Aswad ibn Qays: he heard Jundub say: "Jibril was late in coming to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so the polytheists said: 'Muhammad has been forsaken.' So Allah revealed: ﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it is still, your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you﴾" [[This narration is in Muslim and al-Tirmidhi.]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj and Amr ibn Abdullah [[In A: "Amr ibn Abdullah ibn Abdullah al-Awdi."]] al-Awdi related to us, both saying: Abu Usamah related to us, Sufyan related to me, al-Aswad ibn Qays related to me, that he heard Jundub say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was struck by a stone on his finger, and he said:

"Are you but a finger that bled,
and in the way of Allah what you have suffered?"

He said: So he remained a night or two or three without rising, and a woman said to him: "I do not see your devil except that he has forsaken you [[In M: "has forsaken you."]]." Then there was revealed: ﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it is still, your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you﴾. The wording is that of Abu Sa'id.

It has been said: this woman was Umm Jamil, the wife of Abu Lahab. It is also mentioned that his finger, upon him be peace, bled. As for his statement, this verse which happened to be metrical, it is established in the two Sahihs [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (2802); Sahih Muslim, no. (1796).]]. But what is strange here is making it the cause of his ceasing to pray at night and the descent of this surah. As for what Ibn Jarir related:

Ibn Abi al-Shawarib related to us, Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad related to us, Sulayman al-Shaybani related to us, from Abd Allah ibn Shaddad: that Khadijah said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "I do not see your Lord except that He has become averse to you." So Allah revealed: ﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it is still, your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you﴾.

He also said: Abu Kurayb related to us, Waki' related to us, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, who said: Jibril was late with the Prophet (ﷺ), so he grieved greatly, and Khadijah said: "I see that your Lord has become averse to you, given what we see of your grief." He said: He said to him this surah: ﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it is still﴾.

Al-Awfi related from Ibn Abbas: When the Qur'an was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Jibril was late for days, so he was distressed by this, and the polytheists said: "His Lord has forsaken him and detested him." So Allah revealed: ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you﴾.

This is an oath by Him, exalted is He, by the morning brightness and what He placed in it of light, ﴿and by the night when it is still﴾, i.e., when it becomes calm and dark and black. This was said by Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, Ibn Zayd and others. This is clear evidence of the power of the Creator of this and that, as He said: ﴿By the night when it covers, and by the day when it appears in brightness﴾ [al-Layl: 1, 2], and He said: ﴿He is the Splitter of the dawn, and has made the night for rest, and the sun and the moon for reckoning. That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾ [al-An'am: 96].

* *

His statement: ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you﴾, i.e., He has not left you; ﴿nor has He detested you﴾, i.e., He has not hated you; ﴿And the Hereafter is better for you than the first﴾, i.e., the Abode of the Hereafter is better for you than this abode. For this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was the most ascetic of people regarding this world, and the greatest in casting it aside, as is well known [necessarily] [[addition from M.]] from his biography. When, upon him be peace, was given the choice at the end of his life between remaining in this world until its end and then Paradise, or proceeding to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, he chose what is with Allah over this lowly world.

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid related to us, al-Mas'udi related to us, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, from Alqamah, from Abd Allah, that is Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) lay down on a mat, and it left its mark on his side. When he awoke, I began to wipe his side and said: "O Messenger of Allah, would you not let us know so that we could spread something for you over the mat?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "What have I to do with this world? My likeness and the likeness of this world is that of a rider who rests in the shade of a tree, then goes on and leaves it."

It was related by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, from the hadith of al-Mas'udi with it [[al-Musnad (1/391); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (2377); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (4109).]]. Al-Tirmidhi said: hasan sahih.

* *

His statement: ﴿And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be content﴾, i.e., in the Hereafter He will give him until he is pleased regarding his community, and in what He has prepared for him of honour, and of its totality is the river of Kawthar, whose banks are domes of hollow pearls, and whose clay is [of] [[addition from A.]] pungent musk, as will come.

Imam Abu Umar al-Awza'i said, from Isma'il ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Abi al-Muhajir al-Makhzumi, from Ali ibn Abd Allah ibn Abbas, from his father, who said: What would be opened for his community after him was displayed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), treasure after treasure, and he was pleased by this, so Allah revealed: ﴿And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be content﴾, and He gave him in Paradise a thousand thousand palaces, in each palace what befits him of spouses and servants. Ibn Jarir related it through this route, and this is a sound chain to Ibn Abbas, and such a statement is only made on the basis of revelation.

Al-Suddi said, from Ibn Abbas: Among the contentment of Muhammad (ﷺ) is that none of the people of his household enter the Fire. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related it.

Al-Hasan said: By that is meant intercession. Likewise said Abu Ja'far al-Baqir.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah said: Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham related to us, from Ali ibn Salih, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, from Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "We are a household whom Allah has chosen the Hereafter for over this world. ﴿And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be content﴾" [[al-Baghawi related it in Sharh al-Sunnah (14/248) through the route of Ibn Abi Shaybah, without the verse; Ibn Abi Shaybah related it in al-Musannaf (15/236) by this route without mentioning the verse, and perhaps its mention occurred in the book of tafsir; Ibn Majah related it in al-Sunan, no. (4082), from Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah, from Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham with it, and al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/262): "This chain contains Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad al-Kufi, about whom there is disagreement."]].

Then He, exalted, said, enumerating His blessings upon His servant and Messenger Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him: ﴿Did He not find you an orphan and give you shelter?﴾ This is because his father died while he was in his mother's womb; and it has been said: after he was born, upon him be peace. Then his mother Aminah bint Wahb died when he was six years old. Then he was under the care of his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib until he died when he was eight years old, and then his uncle Abu Talib took charge of him. He continued to protect him, support him, raise his status, honour him, and restrain from him the harm of his people after Allah sent him as a messenger at the age of forty, although Abu Talib was upon the religion of his people of idol worship. All of this was by the decree of Allah and His excellent management, until Abu Talib died shortly before the Hijrah, and the foolish and ignorant among the Quraysh then pressed upon him. * *

*  *

Qatadah said concerning His saying: ﴿Did He not find you an orphan and give you refuge, and find you lost and guide you, and find you in need and enrich you?﴾ He said: These were the stations of the Messenger ﷺ before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent him as a prophet. Related by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim.

In the two Sahihs [through the chain of Abd al-Razzaq], from Ma'mar, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: "This is what Abu Hurairah related to us, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Wealth is not having abundant goods, but true wealth is the wealth of the soul.'" [[I have not located it in the two Sahihs through this chain; it has come in them through other routes from Abu Hurairah. See Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6446) and Sahih Muslim no. (1051).]]

In Sahih Muslim, from Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "He has succeeded who embraces Islam, is provided with sufficiency, and Allah makes him content with what He has given him." [Sahih Muslim no. (1054).]

Then He said: ﴿So as for the orphan, do not oppress him﴾, meaning: just as you were an orphan and Allah gave you refuge, do not oppress the orphan, that is, do not humiliate him, rebuke him or disgrace him, but rather be kind to him and treat him gently.

Qatadah said: Be to the orphan like a compassionate father.

﴿And as for the one who asks, do not repel him﴾, meaning: and just as you were lost and Allah guided you, do not rebuke the one who asks you about knowledge and seeks guidance.

Ibn Ishaq said: ﴿And as for the one who asks, do not repel him﴾, meaning: do not be tyrannical, nor arrogant, nor foul-mouthed, nor harsh toward the weak among the servants of Allah.

Qatadah said: It means to turn away the poor man with mercy and gentleness.

﴿And as for the blessing of your Lord, proclaim it﴾, meaning: and just as you were poor and in need and Allah enriched you, so proclaim the blessing of Allah upon you, as is found in the prophetic supplication transmitted: "And make us thankful for Your blessings, praising them, accepting them, and completing them upon us."

Ibn Jarir said: Yaqub related to me, Ibn Ulayyah related to us, Sa'id ibn Iyas al-Juraири related to us, from Abu Nadrah, who said: The Muslims used to hold that among the thanks due for blessings is to speak of them.

Abdullah ibn al-Imam Ahmad said: Mansur ibn Abi Muzahim related to us, al-Jarrah ibn Malih related to us, from Abu Abd al-Rahman, from al-Sha'bi, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said from the pulpit: "Whoever does not thank for little does not thank for much, and whoever does not thank people does not thank Allah. Speaking of the blessing of Allah is thanks, and leaving it is disbelief. Community is mercy, and division is punishment." [Zawa'id al-Musnad (4/278).] Its chain is weak.

In the two Sahihs, from Anas, that the Muhajirun said: "O Messenger of Allah, the Ansar have taken all the reward." He said: "No, as long as you pray for them and praise them." [[I have not located it in the two Sahihs; Imam Ahmad related it in al-Musnad (3/200).]]

Abu Dawud said: Muslim ibn Ibrahim related to us, al-Rabi' ibn Muslim related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: "He who does not thank people does not thank Allah."

al-Tirmidhi also related it from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn al-Mubarak, from al-Rabi' ibn Muslim [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4811) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1954).]], and said: Sahih.

Abu Dawud said: Abdullah ibn al-Jarrah related to us, Jarir related to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: "Whoever is tested with a trial and mentions it has thanked for it, and whoever conceals it has disbelieved in it." Abu Dawud alone related it. [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4814).]]

Abu Dawud said: Musaddad related to us, Bishr [[In A: "Bashir".]] related to us, Umarah ibn Ghaziyyah related to us, a man of my people related to me, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever is given a gift and finds [the means], let him repay it; if he does not find [the means], let him praise it. Whoever praises it has thanked it, and whoever conceals it has disbelieved in it." Abu Dawud said: Yahya ibn Ayyub related it from Umarah ibn Ghaziyyah, from Shurahbil, from Jabir, [but] they disliked it and did not name him. Abu Dawud alone related it. [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4813).]]

Mujahid said: It means the prophethood which your Lord has given you. In another report from him: the Qur'an.

Layth said, from a man, from al-Hasan ibn Ali: ﴿And as for the blessing of your Lord, proclaim it﴾, he said: Whatever good you do, tell your brothers about it.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Whatever blessing and honour from Allah has come to you in the form of prophethood, proclaim it, mention it, and call to it. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ began to mention the blessing Allah had bestowed upon him of prophethood, secretly, to those among his family in whom he was at ease, and prayer was made obligatory upon him, so he prayed.

Tafsir of Surat al-Duha (The Morning Brightness)
It is a Meccan surah.

We have related through the chain of Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Bazzah al-Muqri', who said: I recited to Ikrimah ibn Sulayman, and he informed me that he had recited to Isma'il ibn Qustantin and Shibl ibn Abbad. When I reached "Wa'l-Duha," they said to me: "Pronounce the takbir until you finish with the ending of every surah, for we recited to Ibn Kathir and he commanded us to do so. He informed us that he had recited to Mujahid, who commanded him to do so. Mujahid informed him that he had recited to Ibn Abbas, who commanded him to do so. Ibn Abbas informed him that he had recited to Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who commanded him to do so. Ubayy informed him that he had recited to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who commanded him to do so" [[Also related by al-Hafiz al-Dhahabi in Mizan al-I'tidal (1/145), then he said: "This is a strange hadith, and it is among what was disapproved of from al-Bazzi. Abu Hatim said: This is munkar."]].

This is a sunnah transmitted uniquely by Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Bazzi, a descendant of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, who was an imam in the readings (qira'at). As for hadith, Abu Hatim al-Razi weakened him and said: "I do not narrate from him." Likewise Abu Ja'far al-Uqayli said: "He is munkar al-hadith." However, Shaykh Shihab al-Din Abu Shamah, in his commentary on al-Shatibiyyah, reported from al-Shafi'i that he heard a man pronounce this takbir in prayer, and said to him: "You have done well and you have followed the sunnah." This implies the soundness of this hadith.

Then the reciters differed regarding the place of this takbir and its manner. Some said: one pronounces it from the end of "Wa'l-layli idha yaghsha," and others said: from the end of "Wa'l-Duha." Tafsir of Surat al-Duha (The Morning Brightness)
It is a Meccan surah.

He informed us that he had recited to Mujahid, who commanded him to do so. Mujahid informed him that he had recited to Ibn Abbas, who commanded him to do so. Ibn Abbas informed him that he had recited to Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who commanded him to do so. Ubayy informed him that he had recited to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who commanded him to do so" [[Also related by al-Hafiz al-Dhahabi in Mizan al-I'tidal (1/145), then he said: "This is a strange hadith, and it is among what was disapproved of from al-Bazzi. This is a sunnah transmitted uniquely by Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Bazzi, a descendant of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, who was an imam in the readings (qira'at). As for hadith, Abu Hatim al-Razi weakened him and said: "I do not narrate from him." Likewise Abu Ja'far al-Uqayli said: "He is munkar al-hadith." Abu Dawud said: Yahya ibn Ayyub related it from Umarah ibn Ghaziyyah, from Shurahbil, from Jabir, [but] they disliked it and did not name him. Abu Dawud alone related it. [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4813).]]

Mujahid said: It means the prophethood which your Lord has given you. In another report from him: the Qur'an.

Layth said, from a man, from al-Hasan ibn Ali: ﴿And as for the blessing of your Lord, proclaim it﴾, he said: Whatever good you do, tell your brothers about it.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Whatever blessing and honour from Allah has come to you in the form of prophethood, proclaim it, mention it, and call to it. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ began to mention the blessing Allah had bestowed upon him of prophethood, secretly, to those among his family in whom he was at ease, and prayer was made obligatory upon him, so he prayed.

End of the tafsir of Surah "al-Duha" [and to Allah belongs all praise]. [[Addition from A.]]
